arcs.title: Foundation
arcs.text: The first three forms (Shailputri, Brahmacharini, Chandraghanta) move from origin to discipline to courage. One reading sees this as preparing the ground: begin steadily, practise patiently, then stand firm.

arcs.title: Creation and care
arcs.text: Kushmanda, Skandamata and Katyayani are linked with creation, motherhood and the defence of what is right. This reading connects the middle days with energy turned into life and responsibility.

arcs.title: Transformation
arcs.text: Kalaratri removes fear and ignorance, Mahagauri brings peace and renewal, and Siddhidatri represents fulfilment. These last nights are often described as the passage from darkness to completion.

arcsNote: This three-part reading is one way to see the sequence. A separate and equally well-known tradition divides the nine nights among Durga, Lakshmi and Saraswati. Different communities understand the progression in different ways.

observances.name: Sharad Navratri
observances.description: The most widely celebrated Navratri. It begins on the first lunar day (Pratipada) of the bright half of the month of Ashwin and leads to Vijayadashami, also called Dussehra, on the tenth day. It is the festival most people mean when they say Navratri.
observances.focus: Durga and Shakti, and in many regions the victory of good over evil

observances.name: Chaitra Navratri
observances.description: A spring Navratri that begins on the first lunar day of the month of Chaitra. In many regions it also marks the start of a new year, and it ends with Rama Navami, which celebrates the birth of Rama, in several traditions.
observances.focus: Devi worship, with Rama Navami as the closing day in many communities

observanceNote: Traditional sources also speak of two further Navratris, Ashadha and Magha (sometimes called Gupt Navratri), which are observed mainly by particular communities. The two above are the ones most widely celebrated.

traditions.name: Garba and Dandiya
traditions.description: Nights of circle dances around a lamp or an image of the goddess, with sticks used in the dandiya dances. Garba is also danced by Gujarati communities in many countries.
traditions.emphasis: Community, music and dance as devotion

traditions.name: Durga Puja
traditions.region: Bengal, Odisha, Assam and Bengali communities
traditions.description: The festival centres on elaborate images of Durga that are worshipped over the last days, usually from Shashthi to Dashami, and are immersed in water at the end.
traditions.emphasis: Durga's visit to her parents' home, and art in temporary pavilions

traditions.name: Ramlila and Dussehra
traditions.description: Dramatised retellings of the Ramayana, ending on Vijayadashami with the burning of effigies of Ravana in many places.

traditions.name: Golu or Kolu
traditions.region: Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and nearby regions
traditions.description: Families arrange dolls and figures on stepped platforms in their homes and invite visitors to see them during the nine days.

traditions.name: Mysuru Dasara
traditions.description: A royal tradition of festivities in the city of Mysuru, with a famous procession on Vijayadashami.

traditions.name: Fasting and devotion at home
traditions.description: Many families observe fasts, install a sacred pot at home, sing devotional songs and visit a temple. Customs vary widely between households and communities.

2026.statusNote: Checked against several published calendar websites that agree on the same dates. Those sites publish for India, so confirm with your local mandir, pandit or Hindu organisation in Suriname before relying on the dates for observance. The first tithi (Pratipada) is reported to run until about 21:30 IST on 11 October, which is about midday in Suriname, so the first day is 11 October in both places.
